newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish, Swedish beet planting over-Danisco.
newsitem.headline: Danish, Swedish beet planting over-Danisco.

text.p: This year's sugar beet sowing was successfully completed by end-April in growing areas in Denmark, Sweden and eastern Germany, Danish packaging, food and sugar producer Danisco told Reuters on Wednesday.
"The beet has been sown in Denmark, Sweden and eastern Germany. I cannot tell you any more for at least one month," a Danisco spokesman said.

Denmark's most intense sugar beet plantings take place in the southern islands of Lolland and Falster and Zealand, on which Copenhagen is situated, with more scattered cultivation on the central island of Funen and the east of the Jutland peninsula.
In Sweden, planting takes place in the south.
Danisco, Europe's fourth biggest sugar producer, has a virtual monopoly of sugar production in Denmark and Sweden.
